A perfect place for seafood lovers, and surprisingly one of the best spots for delicious vegetarian food as well. Located conveniently near Gorai Jetty, this restaurant is a great option for family dinners and weekend outings.

Pratap Lunch Home is a great spot if you’re craving prawns or fish. I tried their butter garlic prawns (4/5), tawa surmai fry (4/5), and Chettinad prawn biryani (4/5). It’s a chill place with a coastal vibe and homely food—highly recommend for a quick lunch.
Top Dishes
•	Butter garlic prawns: Fresh and flavorful, hitting all the right garlicky notes without overpowering the seafood.
•	Tawa surmai fry: Crispy edges with balanced spices, showcasing the fish’s natural freshness.
•	Chettinad prawn biryani: Spicy, aromatic, and generously portioned for a satisfying coastal twist.
Vibe and Service
The relaxed, sea-inspired ambience pairs perfectly with the comforting, home-style cooking. Quick service makes it ideal for lunch breaks in the Fort area.

Waited for 15 minutes to get a place.
They serve all sorts of packet Chaknas here like Moong Dal, Chakli, Seng, Chana, Roasted Chana Etc. These are all reasonably priced between 20 to 40.

We order Bombil Fry, Chicken Sukka, Kori Rotti and Neer Dosa & Solkadi
Being married to a Mangalorean and been a regular to Mangalorean outlets back in Kudla I know the taste very well. This was nowhere near sadly. The Bombil Fry being a Maharashtrian special was just oil fried with light red batter rather than Rawa Fry. Killed the appetite completely unfortunately. It was served a small bowl of Coconut gravy which was again very bland.

The Chicken Sukka was too bland. Quantity was ample but the taste was honestly bland. I tried to finish it with the Neer Dosa since Bhakri wasn't available.

Neer Dosa again was served with a small bowl of Coconut gravy as usual bland.

The Kori Rotti being a staple food amongst mangaloreans was a major let down. It didn't have any flavor and even had sasive(Mustard) in it which was unlike of any Mangalorean Outlet. My wife finished it with a lot of difficulty.

The only savior was the Solkadi and it was really tasty and thick. It was too good and cheap at the same time.

Overall verdict is it's a cheap and pocket friendly place. The food was 2/5. Drinks are probably cheap since everyone was busy consuming that. Solkadi 6/5. The staff were always on the feet and ready to attend.

featured_reviews.name: Debabrata Golder
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are a seafood lover looking for an authentic and budget-friendly meal near Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CST), Sandeep Gomantak Hotel is an absolute must-visit.
Getting There & Parking
The restaurant is incredibly convenient if you are traveling by train, located just a short 5 to 7-minute walk from the CST station. I highly recommend that you go by walk only. Because it is situated in a bustling, crowded area, there is absolutely no parking available. Trying to find a spot for your vehicle nearby is a major problem and will only add unnecessary hassle to your meal, so walking is definitely the smartest option.
Ambiance & Service
Despite being a busy eatery, the management does a great job of maintaining the space. The dining area is kept very neat and clean, making for a comfortable environment to enjoy your meal. Additionally, the service is impressively fast. The staff is efficient and attentive, ensuring you get your food quickly even during peak lunch or dinner hours.
The Food
The star of the show here is undoubtedly the authentic Konkan-style cooking. The fish items are perfectly spiced, incredibly fresh, and exceptionally tasty. What makes it even better is that everything is well under budget, offering fantastic value for money without compromising on flavor. If you visit, you absolutely must try the crab—it is wonderfully prepared and easily one of the standout dishes on the menu.
Verdict
Overall, Sandeep Gomantak offers a fantastic, no-frills dining experience that hits all the right notes for coastal food cravings. Fast service, clean surroundings, and mouth-watering seafood make it a true hidden gem. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pangat is one of those places you walk into with high expectations, especially given its reputation for Malvani thalis and coastal favourites. Having been regular patrons for many years, this place has held a certain nostalgic charm for us, which made our recent visits all the more noticeable in contrast.
We sampled a fairly elaborate spread, including their Bombil Thali, Surmai Thali, Prawns Thali, Mandeli fry, along with add ons like the much talked about Crab Lollypop, Bheja Masala, Kalva Sukka, Chicken Potli Kebab, and also revisited dishes we have enjoyed in the past like the keema pattice, bombil fry, and mutton masala.
While the menu continues to promise a seafood lover’s delight, the overall experience, unfortunately, felt average this time around. The Bombil and Surmai fry had the expected crispness, but lacked that depth of flavour and freshness that truly elevates coastal cuisine. The curries across thalis felt somewhat one dimensional, missing the robust, layered Malvani masala profile one associates with Pangat. Even the basics like chapatis and bhakris, which form the backbone of such meals, could be softer, fresher, and more refined.
On a more specific note, the tisrya masala (dry) felt quite chewy, almost rubbery in texture, taking away from what is otherwise a delightful dish when done right. The solkadhi, too, seemed to miss that refreshing kokam forward tang we have experienced here earlier and elsewhere.
That said, what truly stood out and deserves full credit was the service and hospitality. The staff handled everything with genuine warmth, attentiveness, and honesty. From guiding through the menu to ensuring timely service, their effort and intent were clearly heartfelt, and it did make a meaningful difference to the overall dining experience.
Pangat certainly has the foundation of a great dining destination, and perhaps it is just a matter of revisiting the fundamentals. With a bit more attention to core elements like breads, curries, and flavour balance, it has every potential to regain the consistency and charm it was once known for.
For now, a place that still offers variety, but one we hope will soon rediscover the flavours that made it special for us over the years.

Visited Malvani Klub Restaurant at Lalbaugh with my wife, and we were genuinely impressed with the food, service, and overall experience. We ordered the Bangda Thali and Prawns Thali, and both were absolutely delicious. The Prawns Fry served as a starter was perfectly spiced and crispy, while the Solkadi was refreshing and authentic.

The Bangda fry in the thali had that perfect Malvani masala flavour, and the curries were rich, aromatic, and truly reminded us of homely Maharashtrian coastal food. The prawns curry was equally flavourful, and the chapatis were soft and fresh.

featured_reviews.name: Nitant Pandhare
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Coastal Paradise for Seafood Lovers! 🦀✨
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

If you are looking for authentic Malvani flavors in Mumbai, Malvani Klub is an absolute gem. We visited recently and were blown away by the freshness of the seafood and the richness of their traditional masalas.

The Highlights:

Starters: We started with the Fried Bombil and Prawns Fry. The Bombil (Bombay Duck) was perfectly crisp on the outside and buttery-soft inside—just the way it should be! The prawns were succulent, fresh, and seasoned to perfection.

The Thali Experience:

Surmai Thali: The fish was a generous size, well-marinated, and paired beautifully with the authentic Malvani rassa.

Chicken Komdi Vade Thali: The vade were fluffy and hot, making them the perfect companion to the spicy, flavorful chicken curry.

Crab Thali: A true standout! The crab was meaty and the gravy had that deep, soulful coastal spice kick.

Kolambi Bhaat: This was a revelation! Fragrant rice cooked with juicy prawns and a blend of aromatic spices. It’s a must-order if you want a hearty, one-pot Malvani meal.

Solkadhi: No Malvani meal is complete without this. Their Solkadhi was refreshing, creamy, and had the perfect balance of kokum and garlic to cleanse the palate.

The food here is amazingly awesome and truly authentic. The portions are satisfying, and the taste reminds you of a home-cooked meal in the Konkan belt. Whether you're a hardcore seafood fan or a chicken lover, this place will not disappoint!

Recommendation: Go hungry, and definitely don't miss the Kolambi Bhaat!

The food was exceptional, especially the seafood. The tiger prawns were MASSIVE — genuinely some of the biggest prawns we’ve ever seen, let alone eaten. They were cooked perfectly, full of flavour, and without doubt the best prawns we had in India. That’s saying something, especially as we truly believed Kerala couldn’t be beaten when it came to seafood.

Service was attentive and efficient without being overbearing, and the prices were surprisingly good for the quality and portion sizes. One bit of advice: order your starters before committing to mains — the portions are generous and we definitely over-ordered because everything sounded too good to miss (no regrets, just very full 😅).

Overall, Mahesh Lunch Lounge completely lived up to the hype and then some. Incredible food, huge portions, great service, and excellent value. If you’re debating where to eat — go here.

featured_reviews.name: shripad marathe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Just experienced a fantastic meal at the iconic Bharat Excellensea, a 35-year-old gem in Mumbai's Ballard Estate! The restaurant has been recently revamped, and the ambiance is now even more inviting. But the real star is the food!

As a self-proclaimed seafood addict, I was in heaven. I sampled a wide range of dishes, each bursting with flavor and freshness.

The Tom Kha Soup was a fragrant and comforting start. The Prawns Butter Garlic were perfectly cooked and incredibly flavorful. The *Yellow Chili Prawns  packed a delicious spicy punch. The Surmai Masala Fry was a classic done exceptionally well. The Thalasseri Clams were a fiery delight, showcasing the flavors of Kerala. The Rawas Gassi was a rich and creamy Mangalorean-style curry. The Neer Dosa and Appam were the perfect accompaniments to soak up the delicious gravies.

But the real surprise was the Sitaphal Tricones Holige! This innovative dessert was a delightful fusion of Indian and modern flavors. A must-try!

Overall:
Bharat Excellensea is a must-visit for any seafood lover in Mumbai. The restaurant offers a wide variety of fresh, flavorful dishes with influences from across India's coastal regions. The recent revamp has enhanced the dining experience, making it a perfect spot for a special occasion or a memorable meal. Highly recommended!

Ambiance: Simple, soothing, with both indoor and outdoor sitting. Located at Babhai Naka, Borivali.

Our experience: We went in for dinner on a weekday. The place was largely empty and quiet. Took them 20 mins to take our first order despite having only 4 tables being served including ours.

We ordered the following dishes:
• Bombil Fry: The coating was way too thicker and the bombil hardly present. Could barely taste the bombil.
• Prawn koliwada: Again the coating overpowered the flavor of prawns.
• Bangda Thali and Ravas thali: Both thalis were exactly the same with the same fish curry, a tiny serving of prawn preparation, another tiny serving of matki usal in one thali and another random gravy in the bangda thalis. We weren't asked about our preferences for wada, chapati or bhakri. So one thali came with wadas, the other with chapati and on placing the order the third, we were asked about our preference for chapati or bhakri then informed bhakri is probabaly over. So we okayed chapati but were served wadas.

We also ordered another plate of extra chapati which they didnt have and offered wadas but none reached our table even after 2 reminders.

Finally we finished our meals and then asked for the bill which had the extra cost of wadas which we ordered and never recieved and also for the wada in thali which we weren't informed were charged extra but were given as they didnt have chapatis or bhakris.

They did change the bill on being informed.

We also asked for regular water which we recieved almost at the end of the meal after being reminded for the fifth time.

Service: Slow, and confused even when there were just 2-3 tables with people only.

While we understand it was end if the day and hence the food there was over and also probably that is why there were many errors & delays in service. But the overall experience and food were not upto the mark or hype.

Service is friendly,but sometimes can be very slow as restaurant is full most of the time.Waiters are well dressed & courteous.
Restaurant is very clean & follows good hygiene.
Their menu has a few seafood,Mutton & chicken starters.
Then different varieties  of thalis.
We had specially gone there to have good fresh seafood but found the rates too high as they were as per size.
A Surmai orpomfret thali at around 1000/- however big the fish sounds too high so we had to skip them.
We had a Prawn thali which was tasty with vade & had fried prawns not very big,prawn masala,fish curry,sol kadi,vade & rice for 550/- which was good & tasty.
Also had a Mutton thali with vade for 550/- which was also tasty & worth the price having mutton masala,mutton masala ,sol kadi,vade,rice.
On the whole it was a good meal except for the high pricing of fish items. No rice dishes like biryanis are available  on the menu which is also disappointing.
Can visit with family when in lalbaug area.

featured_reviews.name: vinay shenoy
featured_reviews.review_text: Food at Majghar, Lalbaugh was really good, especially the seafood dishes. Taste and quality were satisfying. However, the service was very slow and disappointing. We had to wait almost 45 minutes just for the starters, and there were unnecessary delays throughout the service. Management should improve the service experience.

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Shetye
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very busy place.
We waited for a lot of time but the time was worth it. We fully had one big thali individually because of hunger. Rice bhakri was soft.
Some may even feel expensive but seriously it not the hype, it's truly amazing.

Surmai thali 10/10 (Highly Recommended)
Kolambi thali
Thecha prawns
Bombil fry
Chicken thali

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Rege
featured_reviews.review_text: The food was excellent and fresh fish was served. Their speciality is thali & authentic malvani food. You may have to wait little longer for service. We had ordered crab thali, surmai thali, halwa thali and prawns thali and bombil fry. We loved their bombil fry and surmai thali. Sol kadhi is amazing and really authentic. Overall little expensive but worth every penny.

featured_reviews.name: Pooja Uday Parulekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
You should visit Majghar only if you’re genuinely hungry because the portions here are massive! The food is absolutely delicious and satisfying. It’s not exactly pure Malvani or Konkani cuisine, but more of a fusion with Vidarbha-style flavors, which actually makes it stand out. Every dish has a homely yet rich taste that leaves you wanting to try more.
The atmosphere is lively and comfortable perfect for families or groups. The interiors have a simple, rustic charm and the overall vibe makes you feel right at home. What really impressed me was the staff they’re extremely polite, attentive, and always ready to suggest the best dishes based on your taste.
Overall, Majghar is a place that balances great taste, generous portions, and warm service beautifully. Highly recommended if you love traditional Maharashtrian flavours and don’t mind rolling out full and happy!

featured_reviews.name: Sudhakar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Asked the waiter what the fresh catch of the day was.
Answer: “Everything is fresh.”
Bold claim.

Ordered Surmai, Pomfret and Prawns.
Pomfret actually lived up to the promise — fresh and tasty.
Surmai felt like it had already celebrated a day or two, and the prawns didn’t exactly scream freshness either.

Fish is seasonal. Not everything shows up fresh every day — a little honesty would’ve helped choose better.

Prices are already premium, and then GST plus a surprise 5% staff welfare charge joins the party on the bill.

Good kitchen, but transparency could be much fresher.

customer_updates.name: Aahar Vihar With Prajakta
customer_updates.text:
Disappointed Despite the Hype

Almost everyone recommended this place, so I had high expectations—but I was extremely disappointed.

First, we ordered Prawns Koliwada, and it was extremely oily. Then we tried the crab soup, which had a terrible smell 🤮. Thankfully, the staff agreed to cancel that order.

Next, we ordered three thalis—Surmai, Pomfret, and Bombil. Unfortunately, the waiter mixed up the order and included prawns in the Bombil thali. When we pointed it out, he insisted it was our mistake. After some back and forth, he finally replaced it.

But the replacement Bombil was worse—very oily and a strange light yellow color. It was so bad it made me feel nauseous, but since we had already paid, I forced myself to finish it.

Honestly, I expected so much more. I won’t be coming back.

customer_updates.name: santosh sanap
customer_updates.text: Try boneless chicken and bombil rawa fry. Awwww yummy 😋😋😋

customer_updates.name: Ajinkya Mhatre
customer_updates.text:
Revisited Jai Hind after almost 4 years. Was expecting it to be really good based on my previous visit. Unfortunately, things have gone really south now (no pun intended). For the price that was charged, the food tasted very average and the hotel has really kind of lost it's soul, I think.

Ordered Surmai thali, prawns koliwada and the famous stuffed bombil. Sadly, the quantity / portion size of dishes has diminished along with the quality. Service was painfully slow on a Sunday afternoon and there were a lot of house flies in the dining area as well. Really concerning health and safety wise. Did not feel like a top quality restaurant at all. Management should really rethink the recent changes. And fast!

Would not recommend trying this place out with either friend or family for the next 6-8 months atleast.

featured_reviews.name: Reena Prince
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently was at Jai Hind again with friends in a Wednesday to indulge in some coastal delicacies.

Ambience is simple and busy as always. Service is prompt and minimum waiting managed well. Special mention of Vinod who very politely attended to us with a smile.

We ordered bombil fry,  pomfret thali surmai thali, prawns masala, neer dosa and solkadi. Have to mention that I love the fish preparation here as it just melts in your mouth as you relish it's flavours. No extra coating or oil. Neer dosa is perfectly thin. Solkadi tastes fresh and refreshing. However, one thing I would like to highlight is the requirement for a thick masala or gravy to eat the roti/ bhakri in the thali since there is only one rassa given in the thali which goes good with the rice.

Overall a satisfying experience and it's value for money.

featured_reviews.name: Jaskirat Singh Rangi
featured_reviews.review_text: Best sea food thaali in all of Mumbai. Alway the same taste and flavor, been going to all it outlets since years.

featured_reviews.name: Omkar Bhatkar
featured_reviews.review_text: Tasty fresh fish and seafood offerings in heart of prabhadevi. Seating coukd be more spacious but the taste compensates for it. Absolutely delicious fish. Loved it.

featured_reviews.name: Sushma Mohitlal
featured_reviews.review_text: It’s located on the main road and easily accessible. The staff is very friendly and helpful. They serve authentic Konkan cuisine, and their North Indian menu is equally delightful. The prawns koliwada and butter naan were my favorites—absolutely extraordinary. I’ve also tried the chicken tikka biryani, basa fry, mutton sagoti thali, neer dosa, paneer tawa fry, and butter chicken. Every dish is worth trying.

featured_reviews.name: Affan Dabir
featured_reviews.review_text: Amazing dining experience. This restaurant gives you all kinds of delicacies including veg dishes, non-veg dishes as well as sea food like fish, crabs, prawns, bombay ducks and squids. I personally loved the surmai and ravas gravy with Goa vade. Yumm Yumm.

featured_reviews.name: Akshata Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place for seafood and had a great experience. Ordered 2 Bombil fry, crab lollipop, and a prawns & crab thali. The seafood was fresh and well-cooked, with balanced spices that didn’t overpower the natural flavours.

The Bombil fry was crispy on the outside and soft inside, the crab lollipop was tasty and nicely seasoned, and the prawns & crab thali was generous in quantity and very satisfying. Portions are good, and the pricing is quite affordable for the quality and freshness offered.

Overall, a reliable place for tasty, budget-friendly seafood. Would definitely recommend it to seafood lovers and would visit again.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent Seafood at affordable prices.

The restaurant is located at a 1 km distance from famous 'Ranicha Baug' (Veermata Jijabai Bhosale Udyan and Zoo). For seafood lovers, it's a best choice.
Even on Sunday, there is no wait time, but the service is little slower.

For vegetarians, there are not much options available there (except chinese food) so it's better to go with Thali.

The place is cozy but still because of less crowd, you feel comfortable.

They accept orders from Swiggy, Zomato, and there is a 10% discount on Zomato pay.

featured_reviews.name: tushar alphonso
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Hidden Gem for Seafood Lovers!
Stepping into Restaurant was like discovering a true culinary treasure. This charming, intimate seafood restaurant, though small in size, delivers an experience from the moment you walk in, the ambiance wraps around you like a warm, welcoming net. It's cozy and tastefully decorated, creating the perfect setting for a relaxed and enjoyable meal. You can tell a lot of thought went into making the space feel both elegant and comfortable.

But let's talk about the star of the show: the seafood! Every dish we ordered was simply divine. The prawns koliwada, bombil fry, chicken lollipop, Surmai fry, PRAWNS biryani & Paneer Biryani, Potato Kappa was cooked to perfection, showcasing the incredible freshness of the ingredients. It's clear they pride themselves on sourcing good quality seafood. The flavors were vibrant, perfectly balanced, and truly unforgettable.

The service was also impeccable – attentive without being intrusive, and genuinely friendly.

If you're a seafood enthusiast looking for an extraordinary dining experience in a delightful setting, [Masta Gajali] is an absolute must-visit. It's a small place with a huge heart and even bigger flavors. Highly, highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Akshay Jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text: This restaurant might be famous for non-veg but I really like their veg thali specially kala Vatana Rassa.. Fish dish was good, surmai size was massive for thali, you could taste malvani taste in it but i found the Chicken dish taste bit masaledar. But overall a decent restaurants and good food.

featured_reviews.name: Flycamm Virtual Tours
featured_reviews.review_text: Great place for Authentic Malvani Food. Taste & Quality is Superb. We tried Pomfret Thali. Must visit if you want to try Authentic Malvani Food

featured_reviews.name: Sangeeta J
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had ordered their Bombil Thali and Prawn Samosa through Zomato from their Mazgaon branch. I was highly impressed with the packing and the good portions of the Bombil pieces. The thali was not spicy or overloaded with masala, and the thali set menu was unique from the rest of the malvani restaurants that also sell Bombil thali. The gravies were really tasty and went well with the rice. The chapatis are huge and sufficient to fill your stomach easily.
Eating in a restaurant and getting home delivery changes the entire food experience, but I loved how they took special care for their home delivery order packing it well so that there is no spillage. Prawn Samosa is a unique dish and makes for a nice evening snack. The filling is decent.
Please keep up the good service and quality.
Abhinandan to the management and cooking team ❤️

featured_reviews.name: Ramdas Dange
featured_reviews.review_text: My dinner here was okay, and the service was acceptable. 😊 The food had some good points, but there were also aspects that could be better. The service was also adequate. 💁‍♀️ However, the atmosphere was quite disappointing; it didn't create a pleasant dining experience. 🙁 The overall feeling was just fine. ✨

featured_reviews.name: Prashant Kapadi
featured_reviews.review_text: We ordered a seafood lunch yesterday, including prawns, pomfret, ravas, and chicken. The food was fresh, well-cooked, and nicely packed. The prawns and pomfret were especially flavorful, while the chicken was tender and perfectly spiced. Overall, everyone enjoyed the meal — great taste, good portion sizes, and timely delivery. Definitely worth recommending!
